title: Adequacy of Network Capacity Factor to Address Gap in Transport Cost and Fares
what_it_is: Adequacy of Network Capacity Factor to Address Gap in Transport Cost and Fares

sections.label: Bus and train capacity added
sections.summary: Over five years, over 1,000 new buses and 200 new trains raised capacity about 25%, while commuter demand rose under 10%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: In the last five years, we have added more than 1,000 new buses and 200 new trains to our public transport network.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: This has increased the capacity by around 25%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: But over the same period, commuter demand increased by less than 10%.

sections.label: Government bears public transport infrastructure cost
sections.summary: Government will bear the full development cost of public transport civil infrastructure, about $20 billion over five years, with lower-income transport spending falling from 4.2% to 2.7%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, the Government will continue to bear the full development cost of public transport civil infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: This is estimated to be around $20 billion over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Over the past decade, monthly expenditure on public transport as a proportion of household income for the lower-income group has come down from 4.2% to 2.7%.

sections.label: Service standard in Network Factor
sections.summary: The service standard component is indirectly included in the Network Factor, so if the rail network does not expand while demand grows, the Factor turns negative and PTC asks for fare reductions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: The service standard component, in a way, is indirectly included in this Network Factor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: As I have explained a few minutes ago, for example, if we do not expand the rail network but demand grows, as it happened a few years back, resulting in crowded trains, then the Factor will be negative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: That means everything being equal, PTC will be asking for a reduction in fares.

sections.label: Fares went down in recent rounds
sections.summary: The speaker says that in the last two or three rounds, fares have actually gone down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: They have their hearts in the right place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: That is the reason why you may remember, I hope people remember, the last two, three rounds, fares have actually gone down.

sections.label: Lower-income transport spending falling
sections.summary: Over the last 10 years, the lower-income group's spending on transport out of household income has gone down, from above 4% to below 3%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: That is why both the Senior Parliamentary Secretary and I repeated that point, which I hope Singaporeans appreciate, that over the last 10 years, the lower-income group, when we look at how much they spend out of their household income on transport, it has been going down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: It used to be above 4%; now it is below 3%.

sections.label: Public transport subsidies and infrastructure spending
sections.summary: Government funding to subsidise public transport is about $9 billion, with bus subsidy about $1 billion a year and about $4 billion for replacing old train assets over five years, plus another $20 billion on new infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Indeed, Government funding to subsidise public transport is a significant one, about $9 billion and – I am relying on memory here, and this is a 66-year-old memory; but then again, a 92-year-old memory can be equally sharp as a young one – I think bus subsidy is about $1 billion a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: For trains, over the next five years, we need to spend about $4 billion replacing existing old assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: So, that is where this $9 billion comes from.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: But actually, that is not the full story because, as I have just mentioned just now, over the next five years, we will be spending another $20 billion on new public transport infrastructure, as we are going to continue to expand this network.

sections.label: PTC excluded unreliable system
sections.summary: PTC did not include it because an unreliable system is the time to pump in more resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: One of the reasons why PTC did not include it is because when a system is unreliable, in fact, that is the time to pump in more resources.

sections.label: Rail reliability dealt separately
sections.summary: Rail reliability is important but should be dealt with separately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: In short, rail reliability is important, but deal with it separately.
